subject: Embedding Redwood into AtlasOps Console - scope, branding & commercial
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex@atlasops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood partner intro - embedded integration interest

Ben —

Quick note to follow up from our brief chat at TechCon. AtlasOps is exploring a tightly embedded assistant inside our developer operations console (the panel where customers manage pipelines and alerts). We love Redwood’s latency profile and the idea of an on-prem/private deployment option for regulated customers.

High level asks from our side:
- White-label UI options (theme + logo swap)
- Usage metering + per-tenant telemetry (we need per-customer token usage)
- Offline / air-gapped deploy option for a subset of customers
- Pricing model: fixed license vs. revenue share (we’d like options)

I attached our product brief. Can you confirm who at Redwood we should loop in (tech + commercial)? Would appreciate a 30–45 min sync next week to go over scope, timelines, and any red flags.

Cheers,
Alex Kim
Head of Partnerships, AtlasOps
alex@atlasops.com
Attachment: AtlasOps_Product-Brief.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@atlasops.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood partner intro - embedded integration interest

Alex —

Thanks — appreciated the brief. Looping in Karthik (platform/eng lead) and Laura (partnerships) to scope.

Early thoughts:
- We can support a white-label integration with theming + logo swaps; two integration patterns: 1) SDK + client-side theming (fast) 2) server-side packaged runtime for deeper embedding (longer lead).
- Metering: Redwood can emit per-tenant usage events; we’ll need to discuss retention windows and whether AtlasOps needs raw event exports or aggregated reporting.
- Offline/on-prem: supported via our Private deployment; we’ll surface the implications for model updates and audit logs.

Can you confirm: expected launch segment (enterprise vs. self-serve), target date, and whether AtlasOps will require co-branding on marketing assets?

Attached: initial scope draft from our side (Redwood_OEM_Scope_v0.1.pdf). Proposed next step: 30-minute technical + commercial kickoff early next week (I have Mon/Tue mornings PST).

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Partners — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_OEM_Scope_v0.1.pdf
From: Maya Ramos <maya@atlasops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Kim <alex@atlasops.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood partner intro - embedded integration interest

Ben / Karthik / Laura —

Thanks, Ben. A few clarifications from product:
- Launch cohort: start with enterprise customers (10 pilots) in Q2 2027; later roll to self-serve.
- Branding: primary requirement is a fully branded AtlasOps UX for customers (no Redwood logos), but we’ll have an integration footnote in docs.
- Metering: we need per-tenant hourly granularity and an export to our billing system (CSV or webhook).
- Data residency: EU customers require EU-hosted inference; is Redwood able to pin model hosting by region for a tenant?
- Offline: target is an air-gapped deploy image for on-prem pilot customers — ability to update models via an approved bundle.

Attaching a short list of compliance questions; also happy to discuss NDA before sharing more sensitive architecture.

—Maya
Maya Ramos
Product Manager, AtlasOps
Attachment: AtlasOps_Compliance_Questions.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramos <maya@atlasops.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 12:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood partner intro - embedded integration interest

Maya —

Thanks for the detail. Technical notes / clarifications below (quick summary — happy to go deeper on the kickoff):

1) Theming / branding
- We surface a CSS + theme layer in the SDK; AtlasOps can fully control colors and logo assets. For deeper UX removal of Redwood strings we support a no-visible-branding configuration under an enterprise license.

2) Metering & telemetry
- Redwood emits token-level events grouped by request session and tenant id. We can push these to an AtlasOps webhook or store in S3/GS and hand a CSV export. Retention configurable (default 30 days).
- For billing: recommend webhooks + batched daily summaries for reliability.

3) Regional pinning & data residency
- Private deployment supports regional pinning per-tenant; hosted tenants can be pinned to our EU region. For air-gapped installs, model updates are handled via signed bundles we publish to a secure staging repo.

4) Offline & model updates
- Offline installs will require a small ops agent to apply updates and rotate keys. We can provide signed model deltas and a validation tool.

5) Integration surface & API
- We expose: generation API, embeddings, chat sessions, and admin endpoints for per-tenant quotas. SDKs available in JS and Python.

6) Security / SSO
- Support SAML + OIDC. We’ll need AtlasOps to share an IdP test instance for SSO integration testing.

I attached a quick API matrix that maps features to integration patterns. Please share an NDA and we’ll circulate an internal runbook and SOW outline.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachment: integration_api_matrix.csv

Please find attached AtlasOps’ initial redline of the commercial addendum and a short tech addendum we’d like included. High level asks from legal: payment milestones, indemnity carveouts for third-party model components, and clear SLAs for Private deployments.

We’ve uploaded a DocuSign envelope for a mutual NDA that would allow us to share internal architecture diagrams. Link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456

Elena Petrov

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrov <elena.legal@atlasops.com>, Alex Kim <alex@atlasops.com>, Maya Ramos <maya@atlasops.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2026 13:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasOps - Redwood: draft commercial terms and tech addendum

Elena / team —

Thanks for the redline and the DocuSign link. Action items and proposals from Redwood to keep momentum: 

1) NDA — Ben to sign the DocuSign envelope today to surface architecture diagrams.
2) Commercial approach — suggest we present two options: (A) annual license + implementation fee (fixed) or (B) revenue share: 70/30 split in favor of AtlasOps after a baseline guarantee. We’ll run numbers based on the pilot cohort details you provided.
3) SLAs & indemnities — Redwood proposing standard Private deployment SLA table and a third-party model component carveout; legal and ops should sync to finalize.
4) Technical kickoff items (P0): SSO test IdP, per-tenant webhook for metering, theming package, and pilot deployment plan. Karthik to own technical delivery; Laura to own partner success.

Proposed next meeting: Thu 12/10 10:00 AM PST (30 min) — I’ll send a calendar hold. I’ve created a HubSpot deal and a shared drive folder for joint docs: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ATOPS-2026-054 & https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAtOps-embed-design

Attachments for your review: redwood_oem_pricing_v1.xlsx (high-level proposal).

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Partners — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
